`AutoLink` and `LinkReferenceDefinition` are core CommonMark rather than a dialect, and refusing them refuses the whole document. That is a known gap, not a design position, and it is the next one to close.

The last three are the ones that used to be **mangled**. Each is a plain paragraph to CommonMark whose meaning is carried entirely by line breaks galley turns into spaces, and each holds ordinary markdown prose — a definition, an admonition's body, a callout's sentence. Carrying that verbatim the way front matter is carried would keep the bytes and make the author's own sentences unreviewable, which is a second silent harm rather than a fix, so they are refused with a line number instead. If your file has any of the seven, edit it somewhere else for now.

**Display math is carried, not edited.** A `$$` block — `$$` on its own line, some TeX, `$$` on its own line — keeps its bytes exactly, delimiters and all, and renders read-only like a fence. galley models that the block is _there_ and models nothing about what is inside it, which is front matter's bargain and is available here for the same reason: TeX is not markdown, so there is no prose inside to review and nothing galley could be right or wrong about. Inline `$x^2$` is prose and reflows with the paragraph around it. (Before this, opening a document reflowed a display block into `$$ E = mc^2 $$` on one line, and escaped the underscores in it on the way.)

**A hard-wrapped paragraph still comes back on one line**, and there that is deliberate: soft line breaks inside a paragraph become spaces, so the paragraph reflows. Task-list items, `~~strikethrough~~` and bare autolinks are carried through as literal text and round-trip byte for byte.
